stemMd: A town believes planting a dense hedge beside a road will reduce nearby residents' exposure to traffic pollution. Which finding is most damaging to that expectation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The hedge species is common locally.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The road carries buses as well as cars.

options.label: D
options.textMd: At that site, the hedge would block air circulation and trap pollutants near the homes.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The hedge would take two years to reach full height.

explanationMd: The finding identifies a mechanism by which the intervention could worsen the very outcome it aims to improve. Site-specific airflow can outweigh the general intuition that vegetation reduces exposure.

distractorRationale.a: Familiarity does not determine airflow at this site.
distractorRationale.e: This delays a benefit without showing a contrary effect.
distractorRationale.c: Aesthetic preference does not measure pollution exposure.
distractorRationale.b: Multiple vehicle types do not establish hedge performance.
